name: Sculpsure

lead: SculpSure is a clinic laser that reduces small pockets of fat without surgery. It is cleared by the FDA for several body areas and the chin.
People use it to refine the waist, flanks and jawline. Sessions run about 25 minutes per area and the maker describes no downtime.

paras: Applicators on the skin deliver a 1060 nm laser that heats fat tissue so fat cells are disrupted and gradually cleared by the body [1].
The manufacturer reports no downtime; clinicians can describe the possible side effects. Body-area candidates are described as BMI 30 or under [1]. Treatment is done by licensed providers.

angle.text: SculpSure targets localized fat to slim areas like the flanks, abdomen and chin, giving a more defined contour. Results develop over weeks as the body clears the treated fat.[1][2]

lead: SculpSure is a non-invasive laser body contouring system made by Cynosure, now part of Hologic. It uses a 1060 nm diode laser delivered through applicators placed on the skin to heat fat beneath the surface, with the aim of reducing small pockets of stubborn fat without surgery.[1][2]

People use it to slim areas such as the abdomen, flanks, back, thighs and the area under the chin, to sharpen the waist, jawline and body outline. Sessions are described as lasting about 25 minutes per area with no downtime.[1][3]

The US FDA cleared SculpSure in May 2015 for the flanks, and later expanded clearance to other body areas and to submental fat.[1][2] A 2022 single-site pilot study in 20 adults reported a measurable reduction in submental fat thickness at three months.[3]

paras: The system consists of a console and four applicators that deliver the laser energy to the patient, according to the FDA clearance summary reported by trade sources.[2] The applicators are flexible and hands-free, so several areas can be treated in one visit.[1]

The 1060 nm laser heats subcutaneous fat enough to disrupt fat cells, which the body then clears over the following weeks.[1][2] Cynosure described this as hyperthermic non-invasive lipolysis.[1] Cryolipolysis (fat freezing, for example CoolSculpting) is a different non-invasive approach that uses cold rather than heat.[4]

Cynosure announced FDA clearance for the flanks on May 19, 2015.[1] Clearance for the abdomen, back and inner and outer thighs followed.[2] In October 2017, clearance for submental fat was reported, based on a 57-subject trial with two treatments six weeks apart.[2] Candidates for body areas are described as having a BMI of 30 or less.[1]
Patients seek it for small areas of fat that persist despite diet and exercise, including under the chin, where reducing fat can define the jaw and neck line.[2]

Abstracts presented at the 2015 American Society for Laser Medicine and Surgery meeting reported data from about 100 subjects at two US sites, with a statistically significant reduction in fat layer thickness at six and 12 weeks, as reported by the manufacturer.[1] The submental clearance rested on a 57-subject trial.[2]

A 2022 pilot study in Clinical, Cosmetic and Investigational Dermatology treated 20 adults (19 women, 1 man) with one 25-minute SculpSure session under the chin and followed them for six months. Ultrasound fat thickness fell from 0.51 cm at baseline to 0.46 cm at three months (statistically significant), and was 0.48 cm at six months. Participants who did not gain weight showed significant reductions at one and three months. Adverse events were mild, transient redness and tenderness, with an average pain score of 3.9 out of 10. The authors noted the small sample, single session, no control group and short follow-up.[3]

Press materials emphasise no surgery or downtime.[1] In the 2022 pilot study, adverse events were mild and transient, and no pigmentation change, scarring, fat dystrophy or infection was reported.[3] Treatment is provided by clinicians, and the manufacturer's labelling should be consulted for adverse events.

timeline.event: FDA 510(k) clearance for flank treatment announced.[1]
Expanded clearance for back and thighs; submental clearance reported in October.[2]
Pilot study of SculpSure for submental lipolysis published.[3]
